summary: Iter_20 CRITICAL BUG. Backend regression 17/18 pass (1 skipped due to Gemini quota on end-of-journal photo). All 7 required frontend markers verified present in /app/frontend/app/index.tsx (maxSide=1400 line 491, quality=0.75 line 491, 300*1024 line 500, pass#2 line 540, w*0.75 line 529, 800*1024 line 527, client_max_body_size 25M + reinicia el contenedor nginx line 680). HOWEVER, the compression pipeline is BROKEN on web due to symbol shadowing: `Image` is imported from 'react-native' at line 21, so `new Image()` at line 505 tries to invoke the React-Native Image component as a constructor and throws synchronously with 'TypeError: Image.default is not a constructor'. The try/catch in the fallback input's onChange handler swallows the TypeError and _friendlyUploadError() emits the generic 'No se pudo conectar con el servidor' message (with the TypeError text), so end-users see a misleading network-error banner. Playwright smoke on the preview URL with /tmp/big.jpg (4.15 MB): (a) NO /api/journal/start POST was captured at all — the request never fires because compression crashes first, (b) UI error banner shown: 'No se pudo conectar con el servidor. Detalles técnicos: Image.default is not a constructor. Comprueba tu conexión, o si estás en producción avisa al admin.' — screenshot at /tmp/after_upload.png confirms. The 413-mock smoke consequently also can't reach the fetch layer, so the new nginx-guidance text ('client_max_body_size 25M', 'reinicia el contenedor nginx') was not observable in the running app even though it exists in code. Both the FOTO INICIO DE JORNADA (camera picker) AND the fallback file input go through the same _compressImage helper, so both photo-upload entry points are blocked on web right now.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: `new Image()` throws 'Image.default is not a constructor' because the identifier `Image` refers to react-native's Image component (imported at line 21), NOT the DOM HTMLImageElement. This crashes the ENTIRE compression pipeline on web, so no photo upload can succeed via either the FOTO button or the fallback file input. Both call ocrPickFile → _compressImage on web, so the whole Jornada feature is broken.

SIDE-EFFECT of above: since the TypeError has no `response`, the fallback branch runs and the user sees a misleading 'No se pudo conectar con el servidor…' banner even though the network was never touched. Symptom the user reported ('la imagen es demasiado grande') is likely THIS bug in disguise — the banner text lists the TypeError as 'Detalles técnicos' but the user may have misread it as a size problem.

integration_issues.issue: Compression step throws synchronously before axios is ever called; no request goes to the backend. Both happy path (real 4.15 MB JPEG) and 413-mock verifications are blocked.

action_items: URGENT: In /app/frontend/app/index.tsx line 505, change `const img = new Image();` to `const img = new window.Image();` (or `document.createElement('img')`). The react-native import of `Image` at line 21 shadows the DOM global. Alternative: rename the import — `Image as RNImage` in the react-native destructure — and search-replace every JSX use of `<Image` (~few dozen sites) to `<RNImage`. The window.Image fix is the smallest, safest change (1 character).

AFTER FIX: rerun this Playwright smoke — expected to see the compressor console line '[ocr] compressed 4144 KB → ~500 KB (1400×1050)' and, if the first pass is still >800 KB, a second '[ocr] pass#2 …' line. The POST body captured by page.on('request') should be well under 1 MB. Then re-verify the 413-mock path returns the new nginx-guidance banner ('client_max_body_size 25M', 'reinicia el contenedor nginx').
OPTIONAL: Add an early Platform.OS==='web' assertion for window.Image existence so future refactors surface a clearer error than 'X.default is not a constructor'.
critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx:505 CRITICAL — `new Image()` collides with the react-native Image import at line 21. The iter_20 tighter-compression change amplified this because _compressImage is now called for anything ≥300 KB (down from 900 KB), so almost every real photo hits the broken code path. Simple fix: `new window.Image()`.

index.tsx:491-562 _compressImage — logic is sound (two-pass compression, quality drop, 800 KB threshold). Only the Image constructor line is broken. After the shadow is fixed, expected reduction on a 4.15 MB noisy JPEG is: pass#1 at 1400×1050 quality 0.75 → ~450-700 KB (likely under the 800 KB threshold so pass#2 skipped). For higher-detail photos exceeding 800 KB, pass#2 (1050×788 quality 0.65) will yield ~250-400 KB. Both stay well under 1 MB.

index.tsx:680 _friendlyUploadError — the 413 message is now excellent and actionable (mentions env var, action verb, container). BUT this branch never runs today because the code fails at the compression step first (see #1). Fix Image shadow → the 413 message becomes reachable and will match the iter_20 acceptance criteria.

index.tsx:666-686 _friendlyUploadError — the `!e.response` branch treats ANY non-axios error (including client-side TypeErrors) as a network error. Consider adding `if (e instanceof TypeError) return 'Error interno del navegador: ' + e.message` so future JS bugs surface honestly instead of masquerading as connectivity issues.

rca_of_the_issue: USER BUG (iter_20): 'vale nuevo mensaje de error : la imagen es demasiado grande'. RCA — the client-side compression pipeline added in iter_18 and tightened in iter_20 uses `const img = new Image()` inside _compressImage. In THIS file, `Image` is one of the destructured imports from 'react-native' (line 21), which on web is a React component object with no [[Construct]] internal method. Calling `new` on it throws 'TypeError: Image.default is not a constructor' synchronously. That TypeError bubbles up out of _compressImage's Promise (since the throw happens before any async work), gets caught by the fallback input's try/catch, and is passed to _friendlyUploadError — which, seeing no `err.response`, returns the generic 'No se pudo conectar con el servidor' string with the TypeError text appended. The end user reads this and reasonably interprets it as a size/network problem, and the developer sees ONLY the banner (not the console) so the true JS error is invisible. Verification: adding page.on('console') to Playwright catches the TypeError message plainly ('[ocr] fallback start error TypeError: Image.default is not a constructor at _compressImage'). Also confirmed by static analysis: only one `new Image()` in the file (line 505), and the react-native Image import at line 21 has been present since well before iter_18, but was harmless until iter_18 introduced this call site — likely wasn't caught because prior iterations only exercised very small photos (<300 KB threshold in iter_18 was 900 KB, so many test payloads bypassed _compressImage entirely). Iter_20 lowered the skip threshold to 300 KB and made this crash universal. Fix: `const img = new window.Image();` — 8 extra characters, zero-risk. The 20 MB backend cap and nginx-guidance error message are both correctly implemented and will start working the moment the frontend Image shadow is resolved.
